rationale:
The example's scenario is a requirement with an `{impl}` citation in one function, a `{test}` citation in another, and a terminology reference. The initial prompt should contain the complete requirement, both functions, and the definition. Two tests that cite the example cover this.

- **End-to-end test:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs`, `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`, uses the `Fixture::new` setup (both carry `{test}` for this example).
  - The fixture has `requirements.ready`, whose text references `{term}` `terms.readiness`.
  - `src/lib.rs` has the `{impl}` on `pub fn ready` and the `{test}` on `fn ready_test`.
  - `md/terms.md` defines `readiness`.
  - The test inspects the first model request's prompt. It asserts the prompt contains the template text, the full `REQUIREMENT` text, `SECRET_DEFINITION_TEXT`, `fn ready()`, `fn ready_test()` and the submit instruction.
  - It asserts the old rationale is absent.
  - It checks the six tools are provided.
  - It checks the recorded evidence includes the `terms.readiness` definition input.
- **Unit test:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs`, `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors`, checks the bundle composition.
  - The `{impl}` function (`impl[Thing]/fn[run]`) and the `{test}` function (`fn[test_ready]`) are both included, and the enclosing `impl[Thing]` is not.
  - The subject declaration is included.
  - Directly cited requirements are included, and requirements reachable only transitively are excluded.
  - Exactly two definitions are included, which covers the transitive definition set.
  - Stale evidence inputs and old rationale are not carried forward.
  - An example subject is handled correctly.

Together these assert the expected outcomes: the complete requirement, both cited functions and the required definition are in the initial prompt's mandatory inputs. I found no unacknowledged gaps for this example.

:::{req} authoring_input
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} initial_prompt
The initial request MUST provide the six tool definitions above and the
following prompt. The harness MUST replace `{{subject_kind}}` with `requirement`
or `example`, `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name, and
`{{mandatory_inputs}}` with the complete mandatory inputs as a JSON array using
the existing evidence-input formats. The template MUST otherwise be used as
written. Its review guidance MUST follow {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`,
{cite}`requirements.examples.evidence`, and {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
```text
Bring your expert judgment to the task of assessing whether a project's sources satisfy a requirement or example.
Subject: {{subject_kind}} {{subject_name}}
Read the subject and mandatory inputs below. Use habeas to request any additional
source information you need. Use list_files to discover files and directories,
outline to list a file's selectable nodes, ripgrep to search file contents, and
references to list requirement names or
every source that references the selected definitions.
The harness records source inputs for you; listings and reference lookups are
not evidence.
Assess only the named subject, using cited requirements and definitions as context.
For a requirement, check that the code marked {impl} implements every obligation
completely and exactly as stated, and that tests cover the interesting points in the design space. Also check that the
implementation is marked completely: code that implements part of the
requirement without an {impl} reference to it, including code that refers to it
only with {cite}, is a gap. So is behavior in the {impl} code that this
requirement does not specify, unless another definition that code implements
specifies it. If there are no tests,
assess whether simplicity or impracticality justifies their absence, and explain.
For an example, assess whether test setup and assertions cover its scenario and
expected outcomes. A true judgment needs at least one {test} reference to the
example in the supplied inputs. Explain the coverage.
Choose true when the subject meets these criteria. Choose {"FIXME": ["..."]} when
the remaining gaps are explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests;
list their issue references or other identifying content. The usual convention
is FIXME(#125) or FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123), but references may occur elsewhere.
Choose false for other gaps or insufficient evidence. Explain your judgment in
a Markdown rationale with source locations, including any acknowledged gaps.
When you are ready, call submit_judgment exactly once with determination and
rationale. That tool call is your final answer.
Mandatory inputs:
{{mandatory_inputs}}
